summary:
Farm Adapt is a decision-support tool designed to address two key challenges in crop rotation planning.

1. Adapting to Changing Environmental Conditions: Traditional crop rotation experience may no longer be reliable as environmental conditions change. The tool integrates relevant environmental data for selected agricultural areas to support crop selection and planning across five dimensions: Where to grow, When to grow, What to grow, How long to grow, and What next in the rotation sequence. It also enables farmers to monitor conditions, receive anomaly alerts, and compare different crop rotation scenarios under varying environmental conditions.

2. Addressing Diverse Farmer Needs: Since farmers have different priorities, the tool allows users to customize evaluation criteria and their weights and define constraints according to their individual needs.

The tool supports decision-making for crop rotation. At the beginning of each growing season, it helps farmers select suitable crops for the next season based on available information or recommends an optimal crop rotation sequence.
details:
Project details

Methodology: link

What it does / how it works
Our tool helps Kansas farmers decide what to plant next season on a specific field. It compares winter wheat, sorghum, corn, soybean and fallow in four steps:

  • Suitability: a spatial multi-criteria analysis (SMCA) scores each crop for the field on a 0–1 scale across 13 criteria in six groups: climate, water balance, soil, terrain, soil cover and economic value. Each score compares field conditions from NASA and USDA data with crop requirements from FAO ECOCROP and the Sys land-evaluation tables.
  • Rotation: hard rules remove unworkable options: planting-window timing, user-excluded crops, no same crop twice in a row, and user-defined forbidden pairs. A rotation factor based on a global meta-analysis then adjusts each remaining crop’s score according to what was grown before.
  • Modes: the tool can recommend the next crop only, or a full multi-season sequence between user-set start and end dates. In sequence mode, fallow can fill gaps.
  • Scenarios and alerts: users compare a baseline (the historical average) with warmer/drier and cooler/wetter scenarios. In-season monitoring sends alerts using agronomic thresholds, statistical anomalies, or “decision-impact” thresholds, meaning the point at which the recommended crop would change.

Benefits

  • Turns scattered satellite and soil data into one ranked, explainable recommendation for each field.
  • Shows why a crop ranks where it does, criterion by criterion.
  • Lets farmers set their own priorities (profit, risk, water saving, soil health) and constraints.
  • Warns early when conditions drift far enough to make past experience unreliable.

Intended impact

  • Help farmers adapt crop choices as the climate shifts, instead of relying only on past habits.
  • Reduce yield losses from poorly matched crops or poor crop sequences.
  • Encourage diverse rotations that protect soil and water.

Creativity

  • Combines land suitability with crop-sequence effects in one score. Most tools handle only one of the two.
  • Works for a single season or a whole multi-season plan.
  • Its decision-impact alerts report how much more change would flip the recommendation, not just that a value is unusual.

Factors we considered

  • Climate variability and irrigation versus dryland farming.
  • Soil, water and planting-window limits.
  • Rotation risks, such as pests and diseases from repeated crops.
  • Farmer goals and economics (price, area, base yield).
  • Data latency and resolution, and transparency of every assumption.
